findings.title: contractApproval hashes a different contract than beginAttempt does: only beginAttempt passes the declared supportingContractPaths, so a change that declares both a lane and a supporting contract file has two digests and the two gates are mutually unsatisfiable
stage execute enforces neither the approved contract nor the executable-contract check, while contracts.md C-01, C-06 and C-07 and a docstring in evidence.mjs all say it does
the review lane is the only mutable unhistoried field in an append-only design: spec lane set --lane low --force is self-approving and cheaper than any amendment link
the declared-versus-undeclared boundary is sound, but every change is born with review null and only prose asks for a lane
amendmentAuthority accepts any one independent review for a scope amendment instead of the recorded lane's reviews, contrary to C-07
the dashboard writable() allow-list accepts reserved .md artifacts under verify/, reviews/, amendments/ and migration/original/, which C-02 requires it to reject
the acceptance target includes the task number, so a cosmetic renumber costs a full re-review and fresh evidence with no amendment type that covers it
usage event ids containing a colon collide with the hyphen form once written to disk, so the second import is dropped as a duplicate
